types/utils.ts/Overwrite: only overwrite keys of objects

Overwrite<string,string> resulted in a mangled object type
because the existing implementation iterated over the string
type's keys (e.g. 'charCodeAt')

This commit changes the implementation so that keys are only
iterated and overwritten in the case of objects. Otherwise,
a non-never TWith type will entirely replace TType, e.g.
Overwrite<string, number> results in 'number'.

summary.intent: Fix `Overwrite` so chained procedure inputs no longer mangle non-object types (e.g. `.input(z.string()).use(...)` inferring a garbled object instead of `string`), per the packet's PR title and commit 7dc04a7.
summary.issue_fit: Met. No originating issue exists; alignment was judged against commit 7dc04a7's stated behavior and the supplied packet, which restates the same intent (the PR body is an unfilled template).
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff of both changed files read; all `Overwrite` consumers in `packages/server/src` inspected. Reviewer ran the clone's `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` in `packages/tests` at the head: exit 0, no diagnostics. The new regression test, type-checked against a scratch copy of the merge-base `utils.ts`, fails at its two `strWithMiddleware` assertions (lines 37-38) and passes at the head, so it discriminates. The runtime vitest suite was unavailable by policy. One safety premise (object operands unchanged) was verified: holds.

observations.fact: The `: TType` fallback in the second branch of `Overwrite` is unreachable, so `Overwrite<X, never>` resolves to `never` rather than `X`, which the doc comment's "unless TWith is never" leaves ambiguous.
